title: What the Sleeping Bear Knows
core_idea: Animals that rest through winter show that withdrawing for a season is part of a natural cycle, not a failure; our own quiet seasons may be the same.
text: Somewhere right now, under snow and earth, a bear is asleep. Its heartbeat has slowed. It is not hunting, not building, not proving anything. And no one in the forest thinks the bear is lazy. Winter rest is simply part of how it lives. Many creatures do something similar. Seeds wait in cold ground. Frogs settle into mud. They pull inward, not because something is wrong, but because the season asks for it. Perhaps you are in a quieter season too. Less energy, fewer words, a pull toward home. That may not be a step backward. It may be the slow, hidden work that comes before the next spring.
description: A calm reflection on animals that rest through winter, and the quiet seasons in our own lives.
